pages.text: The largest of n draws from a bell curve is about $(thing)√(2 ln n)$() standard deviations: five for a million draws. Rare events are rarer than average ones - but not as rare as a bell curve alone says. A Galton Board now and then sorts an Entropy Die into a $(item)Large Deviation Shard$(); the Monte Carlo Engine, tilting its samples toward the tail and weighing them back, makes one every time - slowly. A $(item)Black Swan Feather$() - proof the improbable happens - is a shortcut: with it the Pulsed Magnet Lab finds a monopole every time, and an Ergodic Mixer Core becomes a Boltzmann Brain in a tenth of the time.
The $(thing)Black Swan$() itself comes to the Overworld only after a long time - three days or more - in which nothing improbable has happened to you.
